title: API Contract and Backpressure Integration Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook describes the recommended approach to integrating Redwood Inference with a customer's API surface focusing on: (1) API contract expectations, (2) backpressure and rate-control behavior, and (3) verification and signoff gates for go-live. It is intended for Customer Engineers, Integration Engineers, and partner SREs performing production onboarding for Dedicated or Private deployments.

Scope and goals

- Define unambiguous API behavior and error shaping for inference requests.
- Provide a standard backpressure and retry model for SDKs and proxy layers.
- Outline telemetry signals and QBR metrics required to validate stable economics and latency SLOs.
- Provide step-by-step signoff checklist and runbook pointers for escalations.

Audience

- Customer success engineers (CSEs)
- Partner integration engineers
- Customer SREs and platform teams

Prerequisites (must be completed before integration)

| Id | Item | Owner | Evidence required |
|-----|-----------------------------------------------------------|----------------|-----------------------------------------|
| P1 | Customer API contract (OpenAPI / JSON schema) exported | Customer | OpenAPI v3 file (openapi.yaml) |
| P2 | Network connectivity validated (firewall, peering) | Customer infra | TCP port / TLS handshake success from Redwood test runner |
| P3 | Auth and secrets exchange completed | Customer security | KMS key rotation schedule and test token |
| P4 | Baseline telemetry forwarding configured | Customer/Redwood | Metrics and traces forwarded to telemetry endpoint |

API contract: required fields and semantics

- Request envelope: All inference calls must be wrapped with a stable JSON envelope containing: request_id (uuid v4), client_time_iso8601, model_id, prompt, max_tokens, and optional callback_url for async responses.
- Idempotency: For non-streaming requests, include idempotency_key (UUID). Redwood will deduplicate within a 120s window by default.
- Streaming: If client opts-in to streaming, connection must support chunked transfer encoding and handle partial-message boundaries as documented below.
- Error semantics: Use the following mapping for upstream transformers and proxies: 
  - 200: success with payload "choices" array as specified in schema.
  - 429: client throttling/backpressure — includes header X-Backpressure-Delay (ms) and optional Retry-After.
  - 503: transient service unavailability — should trigger exponential backoff.
  - 400: malformed request — do not retry.
  - 402: billing/quota failure (for hosted customers) — surface to CSE and do not retry.

Backpressure and rate-control integration

Design principles:
- Prefer graceful degradation: surface helpful 429 responses with suggested retry timings rather than opaque drops.
- Push rate limits and queue length information downstream with headers for observability.
- Use client-side adaptive throttling to avoid synchronized retries.

Recommended headers and payload fields to support:
- X-Client-Rate-Limit: client-calculated token/sec estimate.
- X-Backpressure-Delay: server-suggested hold time in milliseconds.
- X-Queue-Position: if requests are queued, approximate position (1..N).

Client retry policy (recommended implementation)

1) On 429 with X-Backpressure-Delay: delay = max(server_delay, base_delay), then jittered exponential backoff with cap at 60s.
2) On 503: immediate short backoff, capped retries = 3, escalate to oncall if persists > 2 minutes.
3) On network timeout: retry once if idempotency_key present; otherwise surface to caller.

Circuit breaker guidance

- Implement a rolling window (60s) error rate threshold of 20%. If exceeded, trip the circuit for 30s and degrade to smaller model or CPU fallback where configured.
- Emit a tag metric circuit_tripped=true with dimensions model_id, client_tier, region.

Observability and telemetry (must be enabled)

Minimum telemetry signals to forward to Redwood and customer observability: 
- request.duration_ms (histogram), request.status_code, request.model_id, request.token_count_in, request.token_count_out, request.client_tier, request.queue_position.
- Traces must include: span for auth, span for request_serialization, span for network_call_to_redwood, span for response_processing.
- Logs: sample 1% of full requests including prompt hash and stack traces on errors > 500.

QBR and health metrics

- Monthly SLO targets (customer-facing):
  - P95 end-to-end latency < configured SLA (e.g., 300ms for llm-small, 1s for llm-medium).
  - Error rate (5xx) < 0.5%
  - Cost per request delta compared to baseline < +15%
- Operational metrics for QBR: median latency, tail latency (P95/P99), throttled request ratio, queued-request ratio, percent of retries.

Integration checklist (step-by-step)

1) Validate API contract: import openapi.yaml into a contract validator and run sample requests.
2) Network validation: run connectivity test from customer environment to Redwood endpoint using our test runner (command below).
  - Example: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <test-token>" https://inference.redwood.ai/v1/ping
3) Configure headers and idempotency support in client SDK.
4) Implement retry/backoff per policy and run chaos tests to exercise 429/503 flows.
5) Enable telemetry forwarding and verify metrics ingestion for at least 24 hours.
6) Run load test at 1.5x expected steady-state QPS for 30 minutes and capture metrics.
7) Execute canary: route 1% traffic for 24 hours, monitor SLOs and error budgets.
8) Signoff: Customer success and customer's platform owner to approve go-live using the signoff template.

Signoff template (required fields)

- Customer platform owner name and email
- Test run id and link to results dashboard
- Canary window start/end times
- Confirm telemetry metrics meet thresholds: latency, error rate, throttling
- Incident contact list and escalation path acknowledged

Failure modes, known issues, and temporary workarounds

- Symptom: Repeated 429s with low X-Backpressure-Delay  Workaround: Ensure client respects idempotency and introduce a token-bucket limiter on client side; escalate to Redwood with request samples.
- Symptom: High queue position spikes during bursts  Workaround: Route spike traffic to a lower-cost, higher-latency model variant (configured in rollout policy).
- Symptom: Streaming connections close mid-response  Workaround: Verify intermediary proxies do not buffer/chunk incorrectly; switch to HTTP/2 streaming if available.

Troubleshooting runbook links and play escalation path

- First-line: CSE troubleshooting checklist (internal link) — verify tokens, idempotency_key, and basic headers.
- Second-line: Redwood infra runbook for backpressure (eng-sre link).
- Escalation: If errors persist and customer business impact is high, open P1 with Redwood Support and attach the following: sample request/response (sanitized), ingestion traces, and load-test results.

Rollout and rollback guidance

- Canary configuration: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with minimum 24h observation at each step for steady-state customers.
- Auto-rollback: If P95 latency increases > 2x baseline or 5xx rises above 0.5% for 10 minutes, automatically shift traffic back to previous model or throttle new connections.

Appendix A — sample OpenAPI fragment

openapi: 3.0.1
info:
  title: Redwood Inference Proxy
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /v1/generate:
    post:
      summary: Synchronous text generation
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [request_id, model_id, prompt]
              properties:
                request_id:
                  type: string
                model_id:
                  type: string
                prompt:
                  type: string
                idempotency_key:
                  type: string
      responses:
        '200':
          description: successful response

Appendix B — quick verify CLI

# Basic connectivity check (sanitized token example)
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}s" -H "Authorization: Bearer TEST_TOKEN" https://inference.redwood.ai/v1/ping

Maintenance and review cadence

- This playbook must be reviewed quarterly and after any major changes to the inference runtime or API contract.
- Additions or changes require a review by Customer Success, Eng-Serving-Runtime, and Eng-SRE.
